newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-A$6 bln Australian coal investment boom seen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-A$6 bln Australian coal investment boom seen.

text.p: The Australian coal industry planned to invest more than A$6 billion over the next five years to develop huge new coal mining capacity, the Minister for Resources and Energy Senator Warwick Parer told the APEC coal flow seminar here.
This would expand annual coal export production to about 250 million tonnes, from the present level of 190 million tonnes, he said.
It would involve investment in 34 mines including 21 greenfields mines, he said.
Port and rail infrastructure investment would be on top of this, he said.
Total APEC electricity demand was expected to increase by more than 70 percent between 1992 and 2010, he said.
Electricity generating capacity in these economies would need to increase on average by more than 13 percent from 300 GW to about 1010 GW in 2010, he said.
Electricity demand in APEC to 2010 was projected to increase by 50 to 80 percent, requiring A$2 trillion in investment capital. Much of this would need to come from the private sector.
Coal's contribution to electricity generating capacity was expected to expand to 42 percent in 2010 from 37 percent in 1992, Parer said.

To meet this, the availability of steaming coal to APEC economies would need to increase by more than 900 million tonnes a year, with China to account for 600 million tonnes of that, by year 2010, he said.
This would require an investment of A$200 billion, on top of the A$2 trillion for power infrastructure, he said.
"As the world's largest coal exporter, Australia is gearing up for this expansion in world demand," he said.
Parer also spoke of a need for long-term contracts in coal supply and for a policy of "differentiation" between countries on greenhouse gas emission control.
